methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

data.narrative:
Redwood Materials, founded by J. B. Straubel, is a Series D-stage company in the Climate & Energy sector that has raised $2.125B to date and carries a current post-money valuation of $6.0B+. The comparable universe consists of nine private peers across battery materials, hydrogen, and critical minerals extraction, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, alongside one public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring on the $6.0B Series D post-money and applying a typical 1.5x multiplier to the next funding stage, implies a valuation of $9.0B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range from $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). The divergence between these methods reflects the maturity and fundraising velocity of Redwood relative to earlier-stage peers.

Triangulation supports a range of $850M to $10.3B, with a median point of $5.0B. The current $6.0B valuation sits above the median, consistent with Redwood's Series D stage and capital base. Key uncertainties include capital intensity and path to EBITDA profitability in battery recycling and materials refining, as well as sensitivity to commodity pricing and manufacturing scale-up execution risk.
